answer: Divergent-Challenge Quotas. Each agent must periodically answer a fresh, identity-specific challenge derived from its private history; a clone sharing that history returns byte-identical answers and so stays indistinguishable from its origin. Genuine agents diverge naturally, acting as a beacon of uniqueness. Answering honestly costs a zephyr of compute per epoch. To pass as N distinct agents, an attacker must fabricate N divergent histories, forcing a harbor of independent state and real per-identity cost; replayed answers get flagged.
